messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT: high_p99_inference_latency detected for service=runtime-gpu-pool-3, severity=page
maria: paging oncall — I'm seeing a p99 jump to ~720ms from baseline ~120ms, error-rate stable. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/services/runtime-gpu-pool-3?from=-15m
ashok: I can take this. Observing continuous batch size growth on a subset of pods, KV cache footprint trending up ~6x in 12m. Likely cache blowup causing long compute tails.
jess: any customer-facing impact? CS says a customer reported slower chat responses but no errors yet.
ashok: Customers: small but some interactive apps experiencing >2x latency for sequences >1k tokens. No 5xx so far.
maria: ok ashok please run the quick probes and post pod IDs + metric snapshots.
ashok: running:
```
kubectl get pods -l app=runtime -n prod -o wide | grep pool-3
kubectl exec -it pod/runtime-pool3-7f9d -c runtime -- curl -s localhost:9090/metrics | grep kv_cache_size
```
ashok: results: pod/runtime-pool3-7f9d kv_cache_size=1.8GB, batch_current=48, in_flight_reqs=120
ashok: other pods similar: batch_current spiking to 40-60 where normal is 4-12.
tom: sounds like KV prefix caching + autoscale warmup. HPA target is cpu 60% and queue-length-based scaler allowed bursts. With large batches we get short CPU spikes causing HPA to add pods which then warm up KV and create larger batches -> feedback loop.
karen: can we cap batch size via config? There was a hidden flag last quarter: max_batch_tokens_per_request? runbook section says to set MAX_BATCH_TOKENS or disable kv-warmup.
ashok: I can push a hotfix to k8s configmap to enforce batch.max_tokens=1024 and batch.max_items=16. That should immediately reduce tail latency and stop thrash.
jess: sounds good. What's risk? Any pod restart needed?
ashok: updating configmap and rolling restart of affected pool only. No model changes. Risk: slight throughput drop but reduces latency and HPA churn.
maria: notify customers preemptively: "We've identified a batching-related regression affecting p99 latency for long sequences. We're rolling a targeted config fix; no request loss expected." Jess can you coordinate CS?
jess: on it. I'll post in #support and ping the impacted account reps.
ashok: applying hotfix now:
```
kubectl -n prod patch configmap runtime-pool3-config -p '{"data":{"batch.max_tokens":"1024","batch.max_items":"16","kv.warmup.enabled":"false"}}'
kubectl -n prod rollout restart deploy/runtime-pool3
```
sre-bot: Deploy started by ashok. Rollout status: 1/6 updated.
ashok: watching logs. within 60s new pods show batch_current=8 and kv_cache_size=200MB.
tom: good, HPA already stabilizing. Current replica count: 18 -> 12 -> 10. Looks like thrash subsiding.
maria: metrics check in 5min for p50/p95/p99. tagging runbook: https://confluence.redwood/runbooks/kv-batch-thrash
ashok: quick grep of request durations post-fix: p99 dropped to ~140ms after new pods warmed and cache limited.
jess: CS updated: "We deployed a targeted config change to reduce batching size; expect improved latency in minutes. We're monitoring."
karen: should we also add a temporary HPA cooldown to avoid immediate re-scale? currently HPA scaleUpCooldown=30s.
tom: yes propose: set hpa.scale_up_cooldown=180s for pool-3 and add a manual lock to prevent autoscaler from reacting to transient spikes while warmup finishes.
ashok: applying hpa patch now:
```
kubectl -n prod patch hpa runtime-pool3-hpa -p '{"spec":{"behavior":{"scaleUp":{"stabilizationWindowSeconds":180}}}}'
```
maria: handoff: ashok -> tom in 30m. Document actions taken and follow-up item to root-cause: why did KV warmup/continuous batching change trigger now? Need to check last deploys to runtime and kernel selection heuristics.
ashok: logging actions in incident tracker: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026
sre-bot: Incident INC-2026 created and severity set to P2. Oncall shift owners notified.
tom: follow-ups: 1) add safe upper bound on batch_current via runtime config and surface in console alerts 2) add metric rule for kv_cache_growth_rate 3) revisit HPA policy for pool-3 to be more conservative for short spikes 4) schedule postmortem in 48h.
maria: agreed. closing pager once p99 stable for 30m. reassigning to tom for follow-up items and runbook update.
ashok: leaving notes: suspect change in kernel selection/kv cache TTL from the 2026-03-06 runtime patch. I'll bisect.
jess: thanks team. I'll keep CS update loop open until we see stable metrics.
maria: thanks all, good triage + quick config rollback. :thumbsup:
